nodes.label: Staff Status Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Staff do not self-register. They are created by owners, then activate through standard login with temporary password. Flow: PENDING_ACTIVATION -> ACTIVE -> PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED -> ACTIVE, with DISABLED as terminal. Temp passwords are BCrypt-hashed for login and AES-encrypted for owner visibility.

nodes.label: Session TTL Configuration
nodes.rationale: Multiple session types with distinct TTLs: normal sessions are 24h, remembered sessions 30d, staff activation sessions 5min. Config keys follow pattern auth.{role}.session.ttl.

nodes.label: Product Search Flow
nodes.rationale: Search is search-first, not browse-first. Scope is locked (PRODUCT or SERVICE) per session. AI structures raw query but must not invent product/business/stock/delivery truth. Auto supplier check attaches to search session but does not create customer-visible chat.

nodes.label: Chat-First Service Booking Model
nodes.rationale: Ask Services MVP is NOT a booking calendar — it is chat + structured fixation of a final agreement. Buttons/actions within chat exist to record the result of an agreement already reached in chat, not to replace communication.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Service Maturity Model
nodes.rationale: Level 1 (MVP): request-to-book with desired time. Level 2 (current): confirmed appointment tracking with minimal overlap checks. Level 3 (deferred): full calendar system with masters, resources, schedules, auto slots.

nodes.label: Three-Level Time Model
nodes.rationale: requestedStartAt (customer desired, never changed) -> proposedStartAt (business counter-offer via SUGGEST_OTHER_TIME) -> confirmedStartAt/EndAt (final agreement via CAN_PROVIDE). Only confirmed time creates a booking record.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Search Architecture
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL holds truth (businesses, branches, products, services), Meilisearch provides fast denormalized search index with typo tolerance and ranking, AI (DeepSeek) structures raw query into SearchPlan JSON without selecting businesses or inventing availability.

nodes.label: Anti-Marketplace Ranking
nodes.rationale: Default sort is intent_match, never price_asc. Ranking combines query relevance, style vector proximity, availability signal, distance, data freshness, business activity, and card completeness. Backend computes raw scores internally; frontend receives human-readable match reasons, never raw confidence percentages.

nodes.label: Supplier Quality Signals
nodes.rationale: Internal-only per-business signals for ranking (NOT public display): data_freshness_score, card_completeness_score, confirmation_accuracy, response_time_trend, activity_level. Produce visible badges like 'Данные обновлены сегодня', 'Быстро подтверждает наличие'.

nodes.label: Contact Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: contact_hash uses HMAC for deduplication (one-way). Actual contact values stored AES-encrypted. Frontend receives contactActionId (short-lived token), never raw phone/username unless explicitly marked public.

nodes.label: Semantic Hard Gate (Search V2)
nodes.rationale: Concrete product/service type acts as a hard semantic gate. A smartphone query must not return laptops, headphones, or vacuum cleaners. A manicure query must not return haircuts. Price can move an item into OVER_BUDGET but must never make a semantically wrong item relevant.

nodes.label: Search V2 Pipeline
nodes.rationale: AI intent structure -> candidate load -> semantic hard gate -> price/city constraint scoring -> result section grouping (EXACT, OVER_BUDGET, WRONG_CITY, SIMILAR) -> fallback explanations. AI-inferred category is a semantic signal, never a raw SQL hard filter.

nodes.label: Ask Platform
nodes.rationale: Ask is a search-first local product and service discovery platform. Anti-marketplace: starts from natural language search, not a tightly controlled catalog. Grows in layers from business registration through catalog import, search indexing, AI intent structuring, and fallback requests. One backend serves all clients (Android, iOS, web).

nodes.label: Feature-Sliced Backend Packaging
nodes.rationale: Backend uses package-by-feature with DDD-style modules (api/application/domain/infrastructure), not broad technical buckets. Feature-Sliced Design is a frontend methodology; the backend adapts the slicing idea into clean/hexagonal architecture boundaries with explicit interfaces for cross-module calls.

nodes.label: Distance Calculation (Haversine)
nodes.rationale: distanceMeters calculated only from real customer+branch coordinates via Haversine formula. Returns null if coordinates missing. Never calculated from city name, district text, or mocked coordinates. Sorting by distance only for rows where distance is known.

nodes.label: Membership and Authority Model
nodes.rationale: Business membership has two levels: BusinessMember (OWNER at business level) and BranchMember (STAFF at branch level). Authority is computed at session creation: ROLE_CUSTOMER, ROLE_BUSINESS_OWNER, ROLE_BUSINESS_STAFF. Roles MANAGER and OPERATOR are removed and must not be used.

nodes.label: Business Cabinet MVP Flow
nodes.rationale: MVP sections: Activity, Products, Services, Company/branch profile, future AI Autodump Import preview. Cabinet is production-facing, not mock. Registered businesses, products, and services must persist. AI Autodump cards stay as drafts until business approves.

nodes.label: Entry Point Model (Three Paths)
nodes.rationale: Three distinct entry paths, not three equal registrations: Customer self-registers, Business owner self-registers, Staff are created by owner and activate via login. No /auth/staff/register endpoint exists.

nodes.label: Autodump Draft Approval Workflow
nodes.rationale: AI never publishes live products/services directly. AI creates drafts only. Business approval is mandatory before search visibility. Approved product drafts create Product + ProductOffer + SearchDocument. Approved service drafts create ServiceOffering + ServiceBranchOffer + SearchDocument.

nodes.label: Public Business Discovery (Astana Import)
nodes.rationale: Separate ingestion layer for public business signals from Instagram, Telegram, 2GIS, public websites. Only public signals — no private scraping, no copying full history. Output: BusinessExternalLink records, business candidates, catalog hints. Backend-owned pipeline.
